description:
A kernel needs to name a byte range (a station name inside a chunk, a chunk inside a file) without copying it, pass it to a helper kernel, and sometimes return it.

Proposed: `slice(a, start, len) :: [T]` for any array a. Native: a view {data + start*esz, len} with a bounds check start >= 0, len >= 0, start + len <= len(a) (raise Enum.OutOfBoundsError like a[i]). Elixir meaning: binary_part(a, start*esz, len*esz), which raises ArgumentError on bad bounds, so Elixir mode must raise the kernel's exception module instead (Ops.slice). A slice of an owned array is not owned (it cannot be returned or written). A slice of an input array can be returned once returning input arrays lands (defk-gqk): natively via enif_make_sub_binary over the original term, so the caller gets a sub-binary and no copy.

Design questions to settle before coding (why this is needs-triage):
- Range facts: a slice's length is a new array variable with len_lo/len_lb facts from `len`; writes through a slice of an alloc'd array: allowed or not? (Simplest: not, in this iteration.)
- Does a slice survive a yield? Views are rebuilt from argv on every entry (defk_bind), so a slice must be re-derived from its base array after resume: emit it as a (base, start, len) triple in the frame, not a raw pointer. Same for the misaligned-copy case.
- Interaction with defk-auo (array value semantics): a slice aliases its base; if writes become copy-on-alias, slices of owned arrays need the same treatment.

Blocked by defk-gqk (arrays through branches / returning input arrays) for the return path only; views as local values can land first.

Done when: slice works as a local value and as a helper-kernel argument, survives forced yields (resume tests), agrees with Elixir mode under the agreement properties, and returning a slice of an input array yields a sub-binary with no copy (checked with :erlang.binary_referenced? style tests or binary.referenced_byte_size).

comments.text: Note from defk-gqk (merged 2026-10-12): an array local that holds an input view (from a branch) is re-bound on resume by exact data-pointer match against the inputs as saved at the yield (resume_block/3, priv/defk_runtime.h). That relies on there being no sub-array views: a slice must be re-bound by offset from its input (store input index + offset, or match by range), and returning a slice must not be mistaken for returning the input (view_term/3 matches data and length).

title: Sub-array views: slice(a, start, len) as a zero-copy [T] value
